title: Smoked Chicken Quarters with White Sauce
displayTitle: Smoked Chicken Quarters with White Sauce
seoTitle: Smoked Chicken Quarters with White Sauce | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Smoke it, sauce it, finish hot — holds well between calls
subtitle: Alabama-style tangy sauce, char finish, and potato salad for ten
description: Chicken quarters ride a steady 275°F smoke, then get kissed over hotter heat to tighten the skin. Serve with a punchy white sauce and a tray of potato salad.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Smoked Chicken Quarters with White Sauce in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Season the quarters
steps.instruction: Mix salt, pepper, paprika, garlic, onion powder, and brown sugar. Pat chicken dry and season heavily on all sides. Let sit 15–20 minutes while smoker heats. Target 165°F at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Smoke steady
steps.instruction: Heat smoker to 275°F. Smoke chicken skin-side up until the thickest thigh hits 175–180°F and juices run clear, about 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Make the white sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk mayo, vinegar, lemon juice, horseradish, mustard, cayenne, and a pinch of salt. Chill until service; it tightens up and tastes better cold. Plan about 6 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Optional crisp finish
steps.instruction: If skin needs help, finish chicken over a hot grill (450°F) 2–3 minutes skin-side down. Don’t burn the sugar in the rub—move to indirect if it flares. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Potato salad (fast tray method)
steps.instruction: Boil potatoes in salted water until tender. Drain, cool 10 minutes, then toss with 3/4 cup of the white sauce, celery, onion, and pickles. Salt to taste. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Tonight’s board
steps.instruction: Tray of smoked quarters, white sauce on the side, potato salad, and extra napkins. Call temps: chicken is pulled at 175–180°F for dark meat tenderness. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Pull meat off bones for wraps or quesadillas. Reheat covered in a 325°F oven until hot; keep sauce cold. Plan about 4 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Dark meat wants higher temps—175–180°F eats tender; 165°F can be chewy.
Sauce stays clean: never brush raw chicken with the serving sauce.
If the skin is rubbery, it needs heat, not time.
tonightSpread: Chicken tray with tongs; sauce bottle; potato salad in a cold pan on ice.
leftovers: Chop into a quick chicken salad.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Quarters are cheap, forgiving, and they feed ten without fuss. White sauce cuts the smoke and keeps the plate from feeling heavy.
mealPrepNotes: Season early. Smoke until done, then hold in a covered pan at 170°F. Crisp skin right before service if you have the time.
substitutions: No horseradish? Use 1 tsp garlic + extra mustard for bite.
